correctness.rationale: For all integers m,n>=2 and every real t in [1,2], the scalar formula follows from the complete, already-known tight-graph vertices and the exact pairwise variance identity ab(t-1)^2+z(C-z), with all endpoint and degenerate patterns included. The Hilbert upper bound follows by decomposing total centered variance into two within-part variances and squared centroid separation; their three constraints form a triangle linear program. Orthogonal regular simplices attain the LP optimum, proving sharpness with target dimension N-1. The conditions forcing all cross distances exactly one and the rank at the first threshold follow from equality in summed distance inequalities and Gram-rank uniqueness. Strict scalar/Hilbert separation for t<2 is proven by the impossibility of nonconstant scalar same-part values under cross-distance-one saturation; endpoint parity follows from optimal two-level counts. For balanced even part sizes calculus gives the unique maximum gap. A stand-alone exact rational checker reproduced 6 signed full-polytope examples, 560 independent LP tests, 144 endpoint parity cases, and 40 balanced examples, supporting but not substituting for the universal proof.

originality.rationale: The exact invariant of scalar Lipschitz spread comes from 2009 graph-spread research; its primary target is random graph spread. The 2026 published bipartite snowflake facet theorem has the exact metric and supplies the known four-level scalar extreme potentials, explicitly credited here; it does not optimize Hilbert variance or classify the scalar-Hilbert gap. Robertson (2023) has the isometric Hilbert embedding threshold t0 for bipartite snowflakes, also expressly credited, but no one-sided maximum variance above the isometry threshold, no second collapse threshold t1 and no sharp scalar comparison. An accessible earlier scalar complete-multipartite result already covers the t=2 scalar endpoint; that case is credited, not newly claimed. Independent mathematical audit and exhaustive bibliographic uniqueness are not claimed.

value.rationale: The exact optimized scalar and Hilbert variances are natural metric-spread invariants over all m,n>=2 and a continuous family of metrics. Their difference has a sharp strict/equality classification, including a parity obstruction at the graph endpoint and a unique worst-case deformation for balanced even sizes. The Hilbert optimum exhibits qualitatively different isometric, coincident-centroid and single-part collapse phases; an explicit all-size finite scalar lattice expression supplies precision that previously known facet counts alone do not present. The result has mathematical motivation independent of reproducibility or raw numerical novelty.
